Subject: RFI: Operational fit assessment — on-prem deployment (IronWall)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking this RFI. To move our procurement review forward we need a concise operational-fit packet focused on on-prem (air-gapped / VPC) deployments. Specifically we need answers and demonstrable evidence for:

- Operator access model: separation of duties, RBAC, limited maintenance windows.
- Telemetry and logs: what is collected, where it is stored, retention options (default + extended).
- Offline/airgap updates: signed update workflow, patching cadence, and SBOM availability.
- KMS/HSM integration and key rotation controls.
- Network topology: required egress ports, endpoints, DNS usage, and a sample diagram.

Can you provide a single consolidated packet and any supporting runbook snippets or diagrams? Procurement would like this by EOD Friday (local). We may have a short technical touchpoint after we review.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Alex Holm
Sr. Security Engineer, IronWall Systems

Subject: RFI: On-prem deployment operational fit — IronWall Systems (consolidated packet)

Alex —

Attached is our consolidated packet; summary below with direct answers to your bullets. Attachments: RFI-answers-ironwall-20270321.pdf (consolidated Q&A + evidence links), operator-runbook-stub.txt (operator tasks and maintenance windows), network-diagram.svg (sample VPC + air-gap config). Also published to: https://drive.redwood.ai/r/ironwall/RFI-answers-20270321

1) Operator access / separation of duties
- Default model: customer-managed operator accounts integrated with IdP (OIDC/SAML) + role-mapped RBAC.
- Sensitive operations (patch apply, key import/export) require dual-approval: operator + authorized approver.
- Maintenance windows can be scheduled and restricted to specific CIDR ranges; operators can be given scoped, time-limited privilege via short-lived certs.
- We provide a sample operator runbook (attached) that describes emergency-only break-glass and audit steps.

2) Telemetry & logs
- What: runtime metrics (latency, GPU utilization), audit logs (operator actions, API tokens, deployment events), and optional application-level request logs (configurable).
- Storage: telemetry can be pushed to customer-managed S3/Blob storage on-prem or to an on-prem SIEM. Default retention: 90 days. Extended retention policies: configurable up to multi-year via customer storage.
- Controls: PII filtering, anonymization hooks, and redaction rules are configurable per deployment.

3) Offline/airgap updates and SBOM
- Updates are signed with our code-signing key; customers receive the same signed artifact for offline transfer.
- We publish SBOMs for releases; customers may verify signatures and run offline validation.
- Patching cadence: monthly security pushes with optional expedited critical patches. Offline install doc included in the runbook.

4) KMS / HSM integration
- Integration: supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) for cloud telco; for air-gapped deployments we support HSM appliance integrations or import of wrapped keys.
- Key rotation: we recommend 90-day rotation for wrapping keys and support automated rotation workflows for cloud-managed KMS; offline rotation workflows documented for air-gapped environments.

5) Network topology / egress
- Required outbound endpoints are limited to our signing and telemetry ingestion endpoints and optional marketplace connectors; full list in the attached network diagram and appendix.
- For fully sealed installs, telemetry endpoints can be disabled; signed artifacts are transferred via customer-controlled media.

Appendix & evidence links in the PDF: SBOM sample excerpt, signed update manifest example, operator audit sample, and a short capture of our telemetry schema. HubSpot record: HS-82943.

If you want, we can join a 30-minute technical call to walk through the packet and address one-off integration constraints. Proposed times (PT): Thu 10:00–12:00 or Fri 14:00–16:00 — tell us what works.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
